Call highlights (customer requirements)
- Latency targets: p50 ~50ms for short prompts, p95 target <=250ms for interactive flows
- Throughput: baseline QPS ~30, expected burst spikes up to 180–220 QPS for ~5–15 minute windows during peak traffic
- Prompt distribution: ~80% short (80–140 tokens), ~20% long (500–1000 tokens)
- Streaming: partial-token streaming required for chat UI (cannot hold until final token)
- Concurrency: ability to support ~120 parallel requests during peak without large queuing is important

Open asks for Redwood (please answer by EOD Wed):
1) Confirm whether we can support 120 concurrent requests for the V1 POC under a dedicated pool and what the recommended connection pool sizing is (connections per process / max multiplexing).
2) Proposed per-account rate limits (sustained qps, tokens/s, burst windows) and how we handle graceful throttling/fallbacks (model fallback, degraded QoS).
3) Any additional observable telemetry we should collect during the POC to validate SLOs (token counts, queue time per request, socket reuse metrics).

Attachments: I attached a short traffic profile export from your team (transitpay_traffic_profile.json) — thanks for sharing.

Marissa / Vivek — sketching a technical approach below. I attached a short connection spec and a quick throughput model (conn_spec_v1.pdf, throughput_model.csv) to make numbers explicit.

Quick answers up front:
- Yes, we can support ~120 parallel requests in a dedicated pool if we allocate a reserved capacity footprint (recommendation: a pool of 8 inference workers sized for your typical prompt length distribution).
- Connection strategy: use HTTP/2 multiplexed connections, 8 connections per client host with up to 16 concurrent request streams per connection (safe default); that yields ~128 concurrency per client host under normal conditions. Keepalive: 60s, idle timeout 5m.
- Rate limits: propose sustained QPS 50 (account-level), token/sec cap 40k tokens/sec, burst window 5x sustained (up to 250 QPS) with adaptive micro-batching at the router for 100–300ms windows to smooth spikes. Enforcement: begin with soft throttling (queuing up to 2s) then 429 + model-fallback if queue exceeds 2s.
- Fallback: when queues exceed threshold, switch excess requests to a quantized model variant (smaller memory, slightly lower quality) but keep streaming enabled. That preserves interactivity for most users.

Observability to collect during POC
- Per-request: request_id, prompt_token_count, response_token_count, queue_time_ms, total_latency_ms, model_variant
- Aggregates: p50/p95/p99 latency by prompt size bucket, concurrency over time, socket_reuse_rate, dropped_requests

Risks / notes
- If TransitPay's spike pattern exceeds the 5–12 minute bursts we saw, we may need short-term autoscaling beyond the reserved pool or accept lower p95 targets during extreme events.
- Streaming stalls are often caused by upstream client keepalive/slow-read behavior — recommend a simple client-side watchdog to detect slow reads.

Attachments included: conn_spec_v1.pdf (connection and pool sizing diagram), throughput_model.csv (simulated latency vs concurrency).

Sanjay / Priya — following internal sizing, here is Redwood's proposed starting configuration for the POC. This is deliberately conservative to hit your p95 targets and keep behavior predictable during spikes.

Redwood proposed POC configuration (initial)
- Dedicated pool: 8 inference workers (reserved) sized for your short-prompt median — expected steady-state capacity ~50 QPS, burstable to ~250 QPS via burst credits + router micro-batching
- Connection pool: recommend HTTP/2 multiplexing, 8 connections/client-host × 16 streams per connection = 128 concurrent streams per host. Keepalive 60s, idle timeout 5m.
- Concurrency limit: account-level concurrent requests cap = 120 (soft), enforced by queueing up to 2s; excess beyond queue will receive 429 + automatic model-fallback to quantized variant with streaming kept on.
- Rate limits: sustained QPS = 50, token/sec cap = 40,000, burst multiplier = 5x sustained (temporary up to ~250 QPS) with smoothing in the router (micro-batches of 100–300ms).
- Fallback hierarchy: primary full-quality model for all traffic → if queue/CPU pressure then quantized model (streaming enabled) → if sustained oversub beyond autoscale window, redirect to shared fallback pool with lower SLOs and rate-limited per-account.

Observability we will expose in POC
- Real-time dashboard: p50/p95/p99 latencies, queue time, active concurrency, token rates, and recent 95th percentile by prompt size. We will create a shared Drive folder with sample dashboards (link above).

Next steps
1) Confirm you accept the proposed caps (concurrency 120, sustained QPS 50, burst up to ~250) so we can open a Dedicated pool ticket.
2) Sign MOU (I can send draft) — this will unlock dedicated capacity scheduling and telemetry retention longer than default.
3) Technical kickoff: proposed 2026-09-01. Ben & Vivek will join to walk the infra team through connection guidelines and observability hooks.

If that looks reasonable, we will draft the MOU and include conn_spec_v1.pdf as an appendix.
